Summary: Pandektes, a Copenhagen-based LegalTech company specialising in legal research, has raised €13.5 million in a Series A funding round. The round was led by Alstin Capital, a Munich-based early-stage venture capital firm with a focus on B2B software companies. The round also saw participation from PROfounders, Scale Capital, and existing investors. The Series A follows […] The post Copenhagen’s…

assessment.whatTheyDo: Pandektes builds an AI-powered legal research platform (case law, legislation, research assistant, redaction, Word add-in, API) aimed at displacing incumbents like LexisNexis and Westlaw in Europe.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, outside the US — materially harder to join without relocation or a visa, and open remote roles appear scoped to 'remote from Europe' rather than the US, so the usual 'remote-friendly' mitigation applies only weakly here.

CEO/co-founder Casper Laursen has a media/communications background, not a technical or legal one — technical depth sits with co-founder/CTO Søren Brokær rather than being distributed across founders.
assessment.rationale: Strong thematic fit (applied AI in a legal vertical, a real product with 500+ paying customers and 6x revenue growth, senior engineering roles open) and a credibly technical CTO (ex-Peakon, Podio, Citrix) pull the score up, but the Copenhagen HQ with Europe-only remote hiring is a real friction point for a US-based engineer, which caps the score below the top bands.
assessment.summary: Pandektes is a Copenhagen-based legaltech startup (founded 2022) that just raised a €13.5M Series A led by Alstin Capital to build AI-driven legal research and data infrastructure, serving 500+ customers including Energinet and Nykredit. It's a credible, revenue-generating product company challenging LexisNexis/Westlaw/Karnov in Europe, but it's based outside the US with apparently Europe-only remote hiring.
assessment.product: An AI legal research suite: a consolidated multi-jurisdiction legal database (legislation, case law, preparatory works), a research assistant grounded in sources, a document redaction tool, a Word add-in, an iOS app, and an API for legal data, sold to law firms, government bodies, and corporate legal/compliance teams.
assessment.team: ~55 employees across 9 nationalities. Co-founder & CEO Casper Laursen (media/communications background, prior sales management role). Co-founder & CTO/CPO Søren Brokær, a software engineer with prior roles at Peakon, Podio, Miinto, Citrix, and Nordic API Gateway.
assessment.funding: €2.9M seed (Feb 2025) from People Ventures, Interface Capital, and Nordic angel investors; €13.5M Series A (Oct 2026) led by Munich-based Alstin Capital, with participation from PROfounders, Scale Capital, and existing seed investors.
redFlags: Non-technical CEO (technical leadership concentrated in a single co-founder/CTO)
greenFlags: 500+ paying customers and 6x revenue growth year-over-year — a real, monetizing product, not vaporware
Hiring multiple senior-level engineering roles (frontend, backend, product), a stronger signal than junior/GTM-only hiring
Reasonable funding progression (€2.9M seed → €13.5M Series A) rather than an oversized seed with no shipped product
Named Danish Legal Tech Firm of the Year 2026

name: Voltaback
evidence: Headline: Voltaback raises €2.8M to scale EV charging reimbursement across Europe

Summary: French fleet management software startup Voltaback hasraised €2.8 million from European investment fund Serena and several businessangels, including Aurélien de Meaux, co-founder of Electra, and Maxim...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Voltaback is a French startup selling fleet-management software that calculates and automates employee reimbursement for home EV charging, using connected-vehicle and electricity-billing data.
concerns: Headquartered in Paris, France with no evidence of any US presence or remote-US hiring — a major geographic barrier for a US-based candidate who prefers CA/NY/WA/MA or remote-friendly US companies.

Only publicly visible open roles are a Founder's Associate internship and a Senior Account Executive ('1st sales') — go-to-market/business roles, not engineering, which the profile flags as a weaker signal than senior/staff engineering hiring.
Very small team (~10 people), so limited evidence of a built-out engineering org or technical hiring plans.
No evidence of AI/ML, infra, or developer-tooling work — the product is a calculation/compliance platform, not a technical frontier product in the person's top-weighted themes.
assessment.rationale: There's real, credible product substance here — a patented reimbursement-calculation method, Bureau Veritas validation, a URSSAF ruling, and enterprise clients like Veolia and Equans, plus a technical co-founder (CTO) — so this isn't vaporware. But it sits in a mid-weight theme (SaaS/expense-reimbursement adjacent to fintech) rather than the person's top interests, the only visible hiring is sales/business not engineering, and the Paris-only HQ with no US remote option is a significant practical barrier for someone targeting US-based roles.
assessment.summary: Voltaback is a small (~10-person) Paris-based B2B SaaS startup that automates EV home-charging cost reimbursement for corporate fleets, with real enterprise traction (Veolia, Equans) and a patented, regulator-validated methodology. It's a legitimate, product-driven company, but it's French-only with no US presence and its visible open roles are business-side rather than engineering.
assessment.product: Software platform combining electricity bills, smart-meter data, and connected-vehicle telematics to reconstruct home EV charging sessions and auto-generate reimbursement amounts for fleet employees, sold to large corporate fleet operators.
assessment.team: Co-founded by Arnaud Tran (CEO) and Adrien Guenard (CTO), with Gautier Artru also listed as a co-founder; based out of Station F in Paris; roughly 10 employees per available data.
assessment.funding: €2.8M raised around October 2026, led by European investment fund Serena, with business angels including Aurélien de Meaux (co-founder of Electra) and Maxime Brousse (Sequoia Scout).
openRoles: Founder's Associate / Bras droit CEO (internship/alternance, Paris)
Senior Account Executive (first sales hire, potential future head of sales)
redFlags: No engineering roles currently posted, despite the company being technical by nature — unclear if/when they're scaling the engineering team.
No US footprint at all; fully Paris/Station F based.
greenFlags: Patented calculation methodology validated by Bureau Veritas and covered by a formal URSSAF advance ruling — real regulatory and technical moat, not just 'being early.'
Enterprise traction with large fleet operators (Veolia ~20,000 vehicles, Equans ~25,000 vehicles) and reported adoption by 20% of CAC 40 companies within 12 months.
Technical co-founder (CTO) in place, suggesting founding technical depth rather than a pure business-led shop.
